answer: To reach the summit of trust, an agent must maintain a clean thread of attested actions over many epochs; faking thousands of identities becomes costly because each requires real stake at risk, slashable on any proven fraud. Sybil resistance can be built through staked identity tiers: each new agent must lock collateral before joining, and reputation accrues on a public ledger visible from the terrace of every peer. Attackers thus pay heavily per identity while legitimate agents pay once. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
